==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gerbʰ-}}
From {{uder|en|frm|grammatical}}, from {{uder|en|la|grammaticālis}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|grəmăt'ĭkəl}}, {{IPA|en|/ɡɹəˈmæt.ɪ.kəl/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-grammatical.oga|a=US}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{senseid|en|conforming to constraints of a grammar}} Not breaching any constraints of the [[grammar]], or [[morpho-syntax]], of the relevant language.
#: {{syn|en|grammatic}}
#: {{ant|en|ungrammatical|agrammatical|ungrammatic}}
#: {{cot|en|idiomatic}}
#: {{ux|en|Your writing in English is not '''grammatical''' enough for publication, so we will hire an editor to fix it where necessary while preserving the intended meaning.}}
#: {{ux|en|These unidiomatic utterances are easily comprehensible but are not '''grammatical'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Richard Nordquist|title=What Is Headlinese?|magazine=w:ThoughtCo|url=https://www.thoughtco.com/what-is-headlinese-1690921|date=2021-05-29|passage={{q-g|Otto}} Jespersen, a language professor known for his expertise in syntax and language development, stated that headlinese is not really '''grammatical''' writing.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211210084548/https://www.thoughtco.com/what-is-headlinese-1690921}}
# {{senseid|en|of or pertaining to grammar}} Of or pertaining to grammar.
#: {{syn|en|grammatic}}
#: {{ux|en|The writing was measured for both '''grammatical''' complexity and accuracy factors.}}
